explanations.answer: Some elders and leaders of the priests
explanations.explanation: That's the crew. The LORD says, "Take some of the elders of the people and leaders of the priests…" (Jeremiah 19:1). Elders and priestly leaders are the ones named to go along. Jeremiah gets a jar and some company for the road trip.

explanations.answer: The gatekeepers and the temple singers
explanations.explanation: Good guess if you like a team with a choir, but the text doesn't mention singers or gatekeepers. The LORD says, "Take some of the elders of the people and leaders of the priests…" (Jeremiah 19:1). So the group is elders and priestly leaders. Nobody's warming up their voice for this one.

explanations.answer: The king and his royal officials
explanations.explanation: The king isn't named on this guest list, friend. The LORD tells Jeremiah, "Take some of the elders of the people and leaders of the priests…" (Jeremiah 19:1). Elders and priestly leaders are the ones the text names. The kings of Judah are the ones Jeremiah is told to address (Jeremiah 19:3).

explanations.answer: Judah
explanations.explanation: Judah is it. Jeremiah is told to say, "Hear the word of the LORD, O kings of Judah and residents of Jerusalem." (Jeremiah 19:3). Judah is the kingdom, and Jerusalem is its city. This message has a very clear address on the envelope.

explanations.answer: Moab
explanations.explanation: Moab isn't who this message is addressed to. The LORD says, "Hear the word of the LORD, O kings of Judah and residents of Jerusalem." (Jeremiah 19:3). That line names the kings of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem. Moab doesn't show up in it, friend.

explanations.answer: Egypt
explanations.explanation: Egypt isn't the one being addressed here. The LORD tells Jeremiah to proclaim, "Hear the word of the LORD, O kings of Judah and residents of Jerusalem." (Jeremiah 19:3). The message names the kings of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem. Egypt isn't in that line.

explanations.answer: They abandoned Him for other gods
explanations.explanation: That's the reason the LORD gives. He says, "…they have abandoned Me and made this a foreign place. They have burned incense in this place to other gods…" (Jeremiah 19:4). The text names the cause right there. No guessing needed.

explanations.answer: They lost a battle to Egypt
explanations.explanation: The LORD doesn't mention any battle with Egypt here. He gives His reason plainly: "…they have abandoned Me and made this a foreign place." (Jeremiah 19:4). It's about turning away from Him and burning incense to other gods. Nothing in these verses is about a lost battle.

explanations.answer: They broke a treaty with Babylon
explanations.explanation: Treaties never come up in this passage. The LORD says the reason is that "…they have abandoned Me and made this a foreign place." (Jeremiah 19:4). Then He lists burning incense to other gods and filling the place with innocent blood. The charge is about Him, not about a deal with Babylon.

explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: Careful, this one flips it around. The LORD says the other gods were ones "…that neither they nor their fathers nor the kings of Judah have ever known." (Jeremiah 19:4). So these gods were not familiar family traditions. The statement says the opposite, which makes it false.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: Right, it's false. The LORD says they burned incense to other gods "…that neither they nor their fathers nor the kings of Judah have ever known." (Jeremiah 19:4). So their fathers and the kings did not know these gods. Those are the gods the incense went to.

explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: True, and the LORD is very clear about it. He says it was "…something I never commanded or mentioned, nor did it even enter My mind." (Jeremiah 19:5). That is as plain as words get. He didn't ask for it, and He didn't even think of it.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: It's actually true. The LORD says burning children as offerings to Baal was "…something I never commanded or mentioned, nor did it even enter My mind." (Jeremiah 19:5). So the text says He never asked for this. This is a heavy verse, and the LORD leaves no room to misread it.

explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: True. The LORD says, "…I will give their carcasses as food to the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth." (Jeremiah 19:7). It's a hard picture, and I think it's meant to be. This verse is part of the weight of the warning.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: It's true, friend. The LORD says, "…I will give their carcasses as food to the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth." (Jeremiah 19:7). This comes right after He says they will fall by the sword before their enemies. It's a heavy line, and the text says it plainly.

explanations.answer: Be appalled and scoff at her wounds
explanations.explanation: That's what the LORD says. "All who pass by will be appalled and will scoff at all her wounds." (Jeremiah 19:8). The people passing by react with shock and scoffing. I think this part stings, because the city ends up an object of scorn.

explanations.answer: Stop and help bind up her wounds
explanations.explanation: Binding up wounds isn't in this picture. The LORD says, "All who pass by will be appalled and will scoff at all her wounds." (Jeremiah 19:8). So the people walking by will be appalled and will scoff. Helping isn't what the verse describes.

explanations.answer: Mourn for her and bring her gifts
explanations.explanation: There's no mourning or gift-giving here. The LORD says, "All who pass by will be appalled and will scoff at all her wounds." (Jeremiah 19:8). Scoffing is the opposite of comfort. The city is called an object of scorn in the same verse.

explanations.answer: It can never again be repaired
explanations.explanation: Yes. The LORD says, "I will shatter this nation and this city, like one shatters a potter’s jar that can never again be repaired." (Jeremiah 19:11). That's why the jar gets smashed in front of the men. They see for themselves what a broken jar looks like. Nobody's gluing that one back together.

explanations.answer: Its pieces will be kept as a sign
explanations.explanation: Keeping the pieces isn't what the text says. The LORD says the jar is one "…that can never again be repaired." (Jeremiah 19:11). The point of the picture is that it's finished, not displayed. No museum shelf in this verse.

explanations.answer: A better jar will replace it
explanations.explanation: No replacement jar is mentioned here. The LORD says He'll shatter the nation and city "…like one shatters a potter’s jar that can never again be repaired." (Jeremiah 19:11). The picture stops at the jar being beyond repair. Nothing about a new one.

explanations.answer: Topheth
explanations.explanation: Topheth is the place. The LORD says, "They will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no more room to bury them." (Jeremiah 19:11). It's the same spot in the Valley of Ben-hinnom where Jeremiah was sent. A heavy detail, so we'll let it sit.

explanations.answer: Shiloh
explanations.explanation: Shiloh isn't named in this passage. The LORD says, "They will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no more room to bury them." (Jeremiah 19:11). Topheth is the place Jeremiah has just been standing. That's the name to hold on to.

explanations.answer: Bethel
explanations.explanation: Bethel doesn't come up here. The LORD says, "They will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no more room to bury them." (Jeremiah 19:11). Topheth is the place named in this passage. That's the one.

explanations.answer: Poured out drink offerings to other gods
explanations.explanation: That's it. The LORD says the houses were those "…on whose rooftops they burned incense to all the host of heaven and poured out drink offerings to other gods." (Jeremiah 19:13). So the rooftops held both the incense and the drink offerings. Both were offered to gods other than the LORD.

explanations.answer: Kept watch for the enemy's armies
explanations.explanation: Watching for armies isn't what the text says. It says the rooftops were where "…they burned incense to all the host of heaven and poured out drink offerings to other gods." (Jeremiah 19:13). The second thing they did was pour out drink offerings. Not a lookout post.

explanations.answer: Prayed toward the house of the LORD
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't mention praying toward the house of the LORD. It says the rooftops were where "…they burned incense to all the host of heaven and poured out drink offerings to other gods." (Jeremiah 19:13). So the incense and drink offerings named there were for the host of heaven and other gods.

explanations.answer: The courtyard of the house of the LORD
explanations.explanation: Yes, that's the spot. "…he stood in the courtyard of the house of the LORD and proclaimed to all the people…" (Jeremiah 19:14). Jeremiah went from the valley to a place where people gather. Now the whole crowd gets the message.

explanations.answer: The Benjamin Gate of Jerusalem
explanations.explanation: The Benjamin Gate isn't named in this passage. The text says Jeremiah "…stood in the courtyard of the house of the LORD and proclaimed to all the people…" (Jeremiah 19:14). So the place named is the LORD's house, with all the people there to hear.

explanations.answer: The palace of the king of Judah
explanations.explanation: The palace isn't where he goes. The text says Jeremiah "…stood in the courtyard of the house of the LORD and proclaimed to all the people…" (Jeremiah 19:14). It's the house of the LORD, with all the people there to hear. No royal doorbell to ring.

explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: True. Jeremiah proclaims what the LORD of Hosts says: "…I am about to bring on this city and on all the villages around it every disaster I have pronounced against them…" (Jeremiah 19:15). So it isn't only Jerusalem, because the villages around it are named too. The announcement names the city and its villages together.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: It's true, friend. Jeremiah proclaims what the LORD of Hosts says: "…I am about to bring on this city and on all the villages around it every disaster I have pronounced against them…" (Jeremiah 19:15). The villages around Jerusalem are named right alongside the city. This part of the message reaches the whole area.
